hotel-pre-sale-renovation-three-options-.title: 酒店出售前还要不要改造？先比较三种出售准备方案
hotel-pre-sale-renovation-three-options-.titleEn: Should a Hotel Be Renovated Before It Is Sold? Compare Three Sale Preparation Options First
hotel-pre-sale-renovation-three-options-.description: 酒店出售前是否改造，要看买方出价能否覆盖投入和延迟成本。本文比较现状出售、整改后出售与经营修复后出售，并用假设算例演示净回款比较和收手条件。
hotel-pre-sale-renovation-three-options-.descriptionEn: Whether to renovate before selling a hotel depends on whether the buyer’s offer can cover the spending and delay. Compare an as-is sale, sale after remediation, and sale after an operational turnaround, with hypothetical net-proceeds calculations and stop conditions.
hotel-pre-sale-renovation-three-options-.author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
content: 酒店出售前改造不改造，看这笔钱能不能在目标买方的出价里收回来：会让买方无法接手、融资或交割、整改范围又能在挂牌前定下来的缺陷，整改后再卖；问题出在经营或产品，修复结果能在出售前形成连续的经营数据，卖方也撑得住这段时间的，才考虑经营修复后出售；不属于这两种情况的，尤其是目标买方会按自己的方案翻新或翻牌时，现状出售，把缺陷清单和第三方估算交给买方。依法必须整改的安全事项，不论卖不卖都要办，不放进这三种方案的比较。
想卖酒店的业主常会问：先刷一遍再挂牌，能不能多卖一点？能多卖多少，要看买方认不认这笔钱。下面先说为什么改造的钱不一定进卖价，再给一张三方案表和一套净回款比较方法。
## 为什么改造的钱不一定进卖价？
买方按自己打算怎么用酒店来出价，卖方的改造只有和买方的用法一致，才可能体现在价格里。卖方花出去的钱，买方不会照单承认。

会计准则里有一个可以借用的角度。《企业会计准则第39号——公允价值计量》（财政部2014年1月26日印发，2014年7月1日起施行）第二条把公允价值定义为市场参与者在有序交易中出售一项资产所能收到的价格；第二十九条要求计量非金融资产时考虑市场参与者将其用于最佳用途的能力，第三十一条要求从市场参与者的角度确定最佳用途。这是会计计量规则，不直接决定一笔交易的成交价。本文判断，它提醒卖方：一家酒店值多少，看的是买方能拿它做什么。

上市酒店公司的公开披露也能看到买方的想法。美国上市酒店房地产投资信托DiamondRock在2026年2月27日提交的2025年度报告中写道，其收购策略主要针对它认为能以低于重置成本买入、并有独特增值机会的酒店。同一份报告的风险因素写明，部分酒店的管理合同和特许经营合同期限较长，可能使一些潜在买方却步，并对售价产生不利影响。希尔顿2026年2月11日提交的2025年度报告则写明，会向现有加盟酒店提出物业改进计划，酒店须完成才能符合品牌标准、留在体系内；酒店发生所有权变更时，还要收取相应费用。
本文判断，这几条放在一起看，意思是：找增值机会的买方，要的正是自己动手的空间；卖方按现有品牌标准做的翻新，买方如果计划换牌，可能还要再改一遍。
## 三种出售准备方案怎么选？
先确定目标买方是谁、打算怎么用这家酒店，再看缺陷会不会挡住交易、经营问题能不能在出售前修出结果，三种方案按同一条规则选。

| 方案 | 什么情况下选 | 卖方先备齐什么 | 主要时间风险 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 现状出售 | 不属于下面两种情况，尤其目标买方会按自己方案翻新或翻牌 | 缺陷清单、第三方查勘与估算、维修记录 | 买方按最坏情况压价 |
| 整改后出售 | 缺陷会让买方无法接手、融资或交割，且范围、费用和工期能在挂牌前定下来 | 整改范围、验收文件、付款凭证 | 工期拖过出售窗口 |
| 经营修复后出售 | 问题出在经营或产品，修复结果能在出售前形成连续经营数据，卖方撑得住这段时间 | 修复前后的经营月报、投入明细 | 爬坡慢于预期，市场窗口变化 |
会让买方无法接手、融资或交割的缺陷，指的是买方或它的贷款方会据此拒绝交易、要求卖方先处理，或把它写成交割前提的问题，例如主要设备故障、证照问题、违反品牌标准而可能被摘牌。本文判断，这类问题卖方不修，买方也会把处理费用和不确定性一起扣进报价。整改范围能事先定下来时，卖方自己修，是把买方的不确定扣减换成一笔确定的支出；划不划算，看下一节的比较。范围定不下来的，归入现状出售，把查勘结果如实交给买方。
经营修复针对的是另一类问题。收益管理、渠道结构、成本控制这类问题，修复后体现在经营数据里；本文判断，买方多半会参考最近一段时期的经营结果出价。修复要见效，需要一段连续的经营月报作证据；卖方的资金和债务到期安排撑不到那个时候，这条路就不成立。
## 酒店出售前改造，净回款怎么比？
三种方案放在同一口径下比较净回款和到账时间。净回款等于预计成交价，减去出售前投入、持有期间的净支出，再减去交易费用和税费。持有期间的净支出只计比现状出售多出来的部分，例如晚卖期间多付的利息、整改停用客房少收的钱；现状出售这一项记为零。
成交价和到手的钱之间本来就有差距。DiamondRock在上述年报中披露，2025年2月19日以9200万美元把华盛顿特区城市中心威斯汀酒店卖给无关联第三方，扣除交易费用并按酒店营运资金调整后，净所得约8900万美元。出售前再花一笔改造的钱，这笔钱也要从到手的钱里减掉。
用一组假设数字推演。某酒店现状出售，买方为一项设备缺陷在报价里扣了300万元，预计成交价8000万元，交易费用和税费200万元，约半年成交，净回款7800万元。整改后出售，先花300万元、用三个月整改，假设这三个月多出的持有期净支出50万元，预计成交价8300万元，净回款7750万元，比现状出售少50万元，到账还晚三个月。只看这一组，现状出售更好。
换一个假设，结论会反过来。买方对同一缺陷估不准，在报价里扣了500万元，现状出售的成交价只有7800万元，净回款7600万元；整改后出售仍按8300万元成交，净回款7750万元，多出150万元，晚到三个月也值得考虑。整改的价值，取决于买方本来会扣多少，以及整改能否让原本不敢出价的买方回到谈判桌上。

经营修复后出售也要两边看。假设投入1500万元，修复和爬坡用12个月，之后再用约半年成交，共18个月，比现状出售晚一年到账；这一年多出的持有期净支出100万元。买方按修复后的经营结果出价9600万元时，仍按交易费用和税费200万元计算，净回款7800万元，和第一组的现状出售相同，却晚一年；买方要按自己的方案重做、只出价8200万元时，净回款只有6400万元。以上数字都是假设，只演示算法，不代表任何酒店的价格、费用或改造效果。
## 谁来拍板，品牌和管理方要先问什么？
出售和出售前的投入都由业主决定。管理合同和品牌合同会影响买方能出的价，要在定方案前问清。

委托管理的酒店，管理方可以提出改造建议和预算，但要先查管理合同里出售时合同是否随资产转移、买方能否解约；合同要随资产走的，改造方案应和买方的品牌意向一起看。特许加盟的酒店，先向品牌方书面了解所有权变更时的条件和费用，以及现有改进计划尚未完成的部分由谁承担。业主自营但挂牌加盟的，按上一句办。既无管理合同也无品牌合同的单体酒店，没有管理方和品牌标准的约束，由业主和财务负责人直接按三方案表比较。品牌合同到期前的续约和换牌，另见[本站讨论品牌合同的旧文](https://www.marvelbros.com/zh/knowledge/hotel-brand-contract-expiry-owner-decision-2026-11-05)。
## 怎样先花小钱试，什么时候收手？
动大钱之前，先花小钱做两件事：请第三方查勘估算，再在保密前提下听潜在买方的意见。
第一件，请第三方做一次工程查勘和整改估算，把缺陷清单、估算依据和照片放进出售资料。第二件，在签好保密协议的前提下，请少数几家潜在买方或交易顾问看现状资料，听他们会怎样处理这些缺陷、会不会保留现有品牌和产品。
试之前，业主和财务负责人先写下判断标准：买方意见里，哪些说法算认可整改，哪些算会重做；估算误差多大以内可以接受。具体数值按本店情况定，写进记录，不在试完后改。
出现下列情况，就停下或退回现状出售：多数潜在买方表示会按自己的方案重做；整改范围在查勘中不断扩大，工期可能拖过计划挂牌时间；经营修复的月报连续不及事先写下的标准；卖方的资金或债务到期时间提前。退回现状出售时，已经掌握的缺陷和估算如实交给买方。
## 这套方法管不到什么？
这套方法只回答出售前花不花改造的钱、花在哪一档，不判断该不该卖、什么时候卖。

它不讨论出售物业、股权还是经营权，也不讨论付款方式怎样比较；出售资料怎样整理，[本站讨论数据室的旧文](https://www.marvelbros.com/zh/knowledge/hotel-sale-data-room-document-index-2026-10-22)另有做法。改造期间的施工方式和停业影响，另见[本站讨论改造总成本的旧文](https://www.marvelbros.com/zh/lean/article/operating-hotel-renovation-total-cost-2026-09-20)。税务、法律和估值结论，要由相应的专业人员出具。迈创兄弟C&T可以协助业主把三种方案放进同一张净回款表。

contentEn: Whether to renovate a hotel before selling it depends on whether the money can be recovered in the target buyer's offer: defects that would prevent a buyer from taking over, financing or closing, and whose remediation scope can be fixed before listing, are remediated before the sale; where the problem lies in operations or the product, consider selling after an operational turnaround only if the fix can produce a continuous run of operating data before the sale and the seller can carry the hotel through that period; in cases that fall into neither category, especially when the target buyer will renovate or rebrand to its own plan, sell as is and hand the buyer the defect list and third-party estimates. Safety matters that must be remediated by law have to be dealt with whether or not the hotel is sold, and are kept out of the comparison among these three options.

Owners who want to sell a hotel often ask: if we refresh it before listing, can we sell for more? How much more depends on whether the buyer recognizes that money. Below, we first explain why renovation money does not necessarily make it into the sale price, then give a three-option table and a method for comparing net proceeds.
## Why doesn't renovation money necessarily make it into the sale price?

Buyers price a hotel according to how they plan to use it; the seller's renovation can be reflected in the price only if it fits the buyer's intended use. Buyers will not accept the seller's spending at face value.

Accounting standards offer an angle worth borrowing. Article 2 of Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises No. 39: Fair Value Measurement (ASBE No. 39, a Chinese accounting standard; issued by the Ministry of Finance on January 26, 2014 and effective from July 1, 2014) defines fair value as the price that would be received to sell an asset in an orderly transaction between market participants; Article 29 requires that the measurement of a non-financial asset take into account a market participant's ability to put it to its highest and best use, and Article 31 requires that highest and best use be determined from the perspective of market participants. These are accounting measurement rules and do not directly determine the price of any transaction. This article's judgment is that they remind the seller that what a hotel is worth depends on what a buyer can do with it.

Public disclosures by listed hotel companies also show how buyers think. DiamondRock, a U.S.-listed hotel real estate investment trust (REIT), wrote in its 2025 annual report, filed on February 27, 2026, that its acquisition strategy mainly targets hotels it believes can be bought below replacement cost and offer unique value-add opportunities. The risk factors in the same report state that the long terms of the management and franchise agreements at some of its hotels may deter some potential buyers and adversely affect sale prices. Hilton's 2025 annual report, filed on February 11, 2026, states that it proposes property improvement plans to existing franchised hotels, which must be completed for the hotels to meet brand standards and remain in the system, and that it charges a corresponding fee when a hotel changes ownership.

This article's judgment is that, taken together, these points mean that a buyer looking for value-add opportunities wants precisely the room to do the work itself; a renovation the seller carries out to the current brand standards may have to be redone if the buyer plans to change the brand.
## How should you choose among the three sale preparation options?

First establish who the target buyer is and how it plans to use the hotel, then see whether defects would block the deal and whether operational problems can be fixed with results to show before the sale; all three options are chosen by the same rule.

| Option | When to choose it | What the seller prepares first | Main timing risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sell as is | Neither of the two cases below applies, especially when the target buyer will renovate or rebrand to its own plan | Defect list, third-party survey and estimate, maintenance records | The buyer discounts the price for the worst case |
| Sell after remediation | Defects would prevent the buyer from taking over, financing or closing, and their scope, cost and schedule can be fixed before listing | Remediation scope, acceptance documents, payment records | Works overrun the sale window |
| Sell after operational turnaround | The problem lies in operations or the product, the results of the fix can build a continuous run of operating data before the sale, and the seller can carry that period | Monthly operating reports before and after the fix, itemized spending | Ramp-up is slower than expected, or the market window shifts |

Defects that would prevent a buyer from taking over, financing or closing are problems on which the buyer or its lender would refuse the deal, require the seller to deal with them first, or make them a condition of closing, for example major equipment failures, license problems, or brand standard violations that could cost the hotel its flag. This article's judgment is that if the seller does not fix such problems, the buyer will deduct both the cost of dealing with them and the uncertainty from its offer. When the remediation scope can be fixed in advance, a seller who does the work itself is swapping the buyer's uncertain discount for a certain outlay; whether that pays off depends on the comparison in the next section. Where the scope cannot be fixed, the case falls under selling as is, and the survey results are disclosed to the buyer truthfully.

An operational turnaround addresses a different kind of problem. Problems such as revenue management, channel mix and cost control show up in the operating data once they are fixed; this article's judgment is that buyers will mostly price the hotel with reference to its recent operating results. For a turnaround to pay off, it needs a continuous run of monthly operating reports as evidence; if the seller's cash and debt maturities cannot hold out until then, this route does not work.
## Pre-sale hotel renovation: how do you compare net proceeds?

Compare the net proceeds and timing of receipt of the three options on the same basis. Net proceeds equal the expected sale price, less pre-sale spending and net holding costs, and less transaction costs and taxes. Net holding costs count only the amount above what selling as is would incur, for example extra interest paid while the sale is delayed and revenue lost from rooms taken out of service for remediation; for selling as is, this item is zero.

There is already a gap between the sale price and the cash in hand. DiamondRock disclosed in the annual report cited above that on February 19, 2025 it sold the Westin Washington D.C. City Center to an unaffiliated third party for USD 92 million, and that after transaction costs and adjustments for the hotel's working capital, net proceeds were about USD 89 million. Any renovation money spent before a sale also has to come out of the cash in hand.

Work through a set of hypothetical figures. A hotel is sold as is: the buyer deducts RMB 3 million from its offer for an equipment defect, the expected sale price is RMB 80 million, transaction costs and taxes are RMB 2 million, the sale closes in about six months, and net proceeds are RMB 78 million. Sold after remediation: the seller first spends RMB 3 million on three months of remediation, net holding costs for those extra three months are assumed to be RMB 500,000, the expected sale price is RMB 83 million, and net proceeds are RMB 77.5 million, RMB 500,000 less than selling as is, with the money arriving three months later. On this set alone, selling as is is better.

Change one assumption and the conclusion reverses. If the buyer cannot estimate the same defect accurately and deducts RMB 5 million from its offer, the as-is sale price is only RMB 78 million and net proceeds are RMB 76 million; selling after remediation still closes at RMB 83 million with net proceeds of RMB 77.5 million, RMB 1.5 million more, which is worth considering even though the money arrives three months later. The value of remediation depends on how much the buyer would otherwise have deducted, and on whether remediation brings buyers who would not have dared to bid back to the table.

Selling after an operational turnaround also has to be viewed from both sides. Assume RMB 15 million is invested, the fix and ramp-up take 12 months, and the sale then takes about another six months, 18 months in total, so the money arrives a year later than in an as-is sale; net holding costs for that extra year are RMB 1 million. If the buyer prices the hotel on its post-turnaround operating results at RMB 96 million, assuming the same RMB 2 million in transaction costs and taxes, net proceeds are RMB 78 million, the same as the as-is sale in the first set but a year later; if the buyer intends to redo the hotel to its own plan and offers only RMB 82 million, net proceeds are just RMB 64 million. All of these figures are hypothetical and only demonstrate the calculation; they do not represent any hotel's price, costs or renovation results.
## Who makes the call, and what should be asked of the brand and the management company first?
Both the sale and any pre-sale spending are the owner's decision. Management and brand contracts affect what a buyer can pay, so clarify them before settling on an option.

For a hotel under a management contract, the management company can propose renovations and a budget, but first check whether the management contract transfers with the asset on a sale and whether the buyer can terminate it; if the contract goes with the asset, the renovation plan should be considered together with the buyer's brand intentions. For a franchised hotel, first ask the brand in writing about the conditions and fees on a change of ownership, and who bears any unfinished part of an existing improvement plan. The same applies to an owner-operated hotel that operates under a franchised brand. An independent hotel with neither a management contract nor a brand contract is not bound by a management company or brand standards, so the owner and the head of finance compare the options directly using the three-option table. For renewal and rebranding before a brand contract expires, see [the earlier article on this site about brand contracts](https://www.marvelbros.com/en/knowledge/hotel-brand-contract-expiry-owner-decision-2026-11-05).
## How do you test cheaply first, and when do you stop?
Before committing big money, spend a little on two things: commission a third-party survey and estimate, and then hear potential buyers' views under confidentiality.

First, have a third party carry out an engineering survey and remediation estimate, and put the defect list, the basis of the estimate and photographs into the sale materials. Second, with nondisclosure agreements signed, ask a few potential buyers or transaction advisers to review the as-is materials, and hear how they would handle these defects and whether they would keep the existing brand and product.

Before the test, the owner and the head of finance write down the decision criteria: which buyer comments count as accepting the remediation and which mean the buyer would redo the work, and how large an estimating error is acceptable. The specific values are set for the hotel's own situation and recorded, and are not changed after the test.

Stop, or fall back to selling as is, when any of the following occurs: most potential buyers say they would redo the hotel to their own plan; the remediation scope keeps growing during the survey and the works could run past the planned listing date; consecutive monthly reports of an operational turnaround fall short of the criteria written down in advance; or the seller's cash or debt maturity dates move earlier. When falling back to selling as is, disclose the defects and estimates already identified to the buyer truthfully.
## What does this method not cover?
This method answers only whether to spend renovation money before a sale and at which level; it does not judge whether or when to sell.

It does not discuss whether to sell the property, the equity or the operating rights, nor how to compare payment terms; for how to organize the sale materials, [an earlier article on this site about data rooms](https://www.marvelbros.com/en/knowledge/hotel-sale-data-room-document-index-2026-10-22) offers a method. For construction methods and the impact of closures during renovation, see the earlier article on this site about total renovation cost. Tax, legal and valuation conclusions must be provided by the relevant professionals. MarvelBros C&T can help owners put the three options into a single net proceeds table.
